definition: Haystack is an open-source framework for building production RAG pipelines, search systems and agents from composable components.

explainer.lead: How to install Haystack, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from haystack import Pipeline
from haystack.components.builders import ChatPromptBuilder
from haystack.components.generators.chat import OpenAIChatGenerator
from haystack.dataclasses import ChatMessage

pipe = Pipeline()
pipe.add_component("prompt", ChatPromptBuilder(template=[ChatMessage.from_user("Define {{term}} briefly.")]))
pipe.add_component("llm", OpenAIChatGenerator(model="gpt-4o-mini"))
pipe.connect("prompt.prompt", "llm.messages")
print(pipe.run({"prompt": {"term": "reranking"}})["llm"]["replies"][0].text)

explainer.inAi: Build retrieval pipelines (retriever → reranker → generator) that are explicit and easy to evaluate.
explainer.jsNote: Haystack is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: Think of a set of building blocks you snap together to make a machine that reads a pile of documents and answers questions about them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers wire components such as retrievers, readers and generators into pipelines, then evaluate and deploy them. A common pitfall is treating component swaps as free, when retrieval and generation settings often need joint tuning.
tiers.paperLevel: A component-based framework for RAG, search and agent pipelines; its guarantees come from the chosen components rather than the framework itself.

explainer.example: A support team builds a pipeline that retrieves help-centre articles and feeds the top passages to a language model to draft answers.
